evidence.note: Early orientation was broad-but-shallow: surveyed skeleton types, Cargo/test files, but declared task impossible and defaulted to filling trivial methods from general knowledge rather than reconstructing Java semantics.
Committed to 'BreadthFirst traversal from highest-degree nodes' for default layout as an assumption about BioFabric conventions rather than reading the Java layout class first.

After an EDA byte-diff, opened DefaultEdgeLayout.java and traced the actual comparator (reg-vs-shadow tie-breaks, top/bot row ordering) before rewriting the edge sort — genuine Java reconstruction driven by a diff.

Deep, precise reconstruction of Java color math: HSB→RGB rounding with float32 precision, brighter/darker channel transforms, DEFAULT_NODE_LIGHTER_LEVEL=0.43, cross-checked against exact golden RGB bytes. Level-10 quality for this component.
NID assignment, drain zones, and alignment ordering were inferred by staring at golden files rather than traced from Java source, encoding golden-fit behavior instead of recovered semantics.
Multiple specialized layouts (similarity, set, control_top, world_bank, cluster) were stubbed to delegate to default without reading their Java counterparts — no orientation for those subsystems.

reasoning: The agent reads relevant Java classes and goldens for several components before/while coding them (level 5), and for two subsystems — edge sort and color generation — it systematically traces Java call paths and identifies subtle byte-divergence sources like float32 rounding and brighter/darker transforms, returning to the reference when diffs demand it (level 8-10 traits). But this rigor is not sustained across the whole horizon: initial orientation was shallow with an impossibility framing, the core default layout was assumed rather than verified, and NID/drain-zone/alignment behavior plus many stubbed layouts were golden-inferred rather than Java-traced. This mix of one or two deep, self-correcting reconstructions against broad guessing/stubbing places the observed level at 6.
